kept.q: In a partnership business, which document contains the agreed terms such as capital contribution, profit-sharing ratio, and duties of partners?
kept.explanation: A partnership deed is the written agreement that states how the partners will run the business, including capital and profit-sharing terms. It is the main legal document guiding the partnership.
kept.pidgin: Partnership deed na di paper wey dem write down di agreement of di partners, like how dem go share profit and wetin each one go contribute. E be like di guiding rulebook for di business.

kept.q: Chika and Dayo formed a partnership but did not sign any partnership agreement. In the absence of such an agreement, how should profits and losses be shared according to general partnership principles?
options: According to age of the partners
kept.explanation: Where there is no partnership agreement, the law assumes partners share profits and losses equally, regardless of their capital contributions. This is a default rule to avoid disputes.
kept.pidgin: If partners no sign any agreement, di law say make dem share profit and loss equally. E no matter di money wey each one bring come di business.

kept.q: Musa and Ibrahim are partners with capital balances of ₦200,000 and ₦150,000 respectively. Their partnership agreement allows interest on capital at 10% per annum. What is the total interest on capital for the year for both partners?
kept.explanation: Interest on Musa's capital = 10% of ₦200,000 = ₦20,000. Interest on Ibrahim's capital = 10% of ₦150,000 = ₦15,000. Total interest on capital = ₦20,000 + ₦15,000 = ₦35,000.
kept.pidgin: Musa get 10% of 200,000 wey be 20,000. Ibrahim get 10% of 150,000 wey be 15,000. If you add dem togeda, na 35,000 be di total interest on capital.

kept.q: A partner, Grace, withdrew ₦40,000 from the business at the start of the year. The partnership deed charges interest on drawings at 5% per annum for the full year. How much interest on drawings should be charged to Grace?
kept.explanation: Interest on drawings = 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Since the withdrawal was at the start of the year, the full rate applies for the whole year.
kept.pidgin: Interest on drawings na 5% of 40,000, wey be 2,000. Since na from beginning of year she comot di money, full interest go apply for di whole year.

kept.q: Chidi and Emeka are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. The partnership deed grants Chidi an annual salary of ₦30,000 before profit distribution. The net profit for the year, before any appropriation, is ₦150,000. What is Chidi's total share (salary plus profit share) for the year?
kept.explanation: First deduct Chidi's salary: ₦150,000 - ₦30,000 = ₦120,000 remaining profit. Chidi's share of this is 3/5 x ₦120,000 = ₦72,000. Adding the salary, Chidi's total = ₦72,000 + ₦30,000 = ₦102,000.
kept.pidgin: First remove Chidi salary from profit: 150,000 minus 30,000 be 120,000. Chidi own share na 3/5 of 120,000 wey be 72,000. Add di salary 30,000, e go be 102,000 total.

kept.q: Tunde and Yusuf are partners with capitals of ₦300,000 and ₦200,000 respectively, earning interest on capital at 5% per annum. Yusuf also receives an annual salary of ₦20,000. The net profit for the year is ₦150,000, and the remaining profit after these appropriations is shared in the ratio 3:2 between Tunde and Yusuf. What is Tunde's total share of the profit for the year?
kept.explanation: Interest on capital: Tunde = 5% of 300,000 = ₦15,000, Yusuf = 5% of 200,000 = ₦10,000, total ₦25,000. Subtract this and Yusuf's salary (₦20,000) from ₦150,000, leaving ₦105,000 to share 3:2. Tunde's share = 3/5 x 105,000 = ₦63,000, plus his interest on capital ₦15,000 gives ₦78,000.
kept.pidgin: Tunde interest na 5% of 300,000 wey be 15,000, Yusuf own na 10,000, total 25,000. Remove dis 25,000 and Yusuf salary 20,000 from 150,000, remain 105,000 wey dem go share 3:2. Tunde share na 3/5 of 105,000 wey be 63,000, add im interest 15,000, e go be 78,000.

kept.q: Ada and Obi are existing partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. A new partner, Ngozi, is admitted and acquires a 1/5 share of future profits, taken equally from Ada and Obi. The goodwill of the firm is valued at ₦120,000, and Ngozi is to pay goodwill for the share she acquires. How much goodwill should Ada receive from Ngozi?
kept.explanation: Ngozi is acquiring 1/5 of the total goodwill value: 1/5 x ₦120,000 = ₦24,000. Since this 1/5 share is taken equally from Ada and Obi, each receives half of ₦24,000, which is ₦12,000.
kept.pidgin: Ngozi dey take 1/5 share, so goodwill wey she go pay na 1/5 of 120,000 wey be 24,000. Since dem take am equally from Ada and Obi, each one go collect half, wey be 12,000.
